subject: physics_2
question_text: Define 'power' of a convex lens. What is its unit?

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed p.10 — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked physically: P = 1/f gives dioptre only with f in metre (1 D = 1 m⁻¹); a convex lens has f > 0 so P > 0; the book prints the unit as 'diopter (D)' — the standard board spelling dioptre is used here.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ray Optics and Optical Instruments · 2 marks

steps.label: Definition P = 1/f
lines: The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its
It measures how strongly the lens converges
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write P = 1/f and say f is in metre — the unit condition is part of the definition.
steps.why: P = 1/f is defined so that a stronger lens — one with a smaller focal length, which bends rays more — gets a bigger number. The reciprocal is what makes short f mean high power.
common_mistakes: Using f in centimetre. P = 1/f gives dioptre only when f is in metre.
Writing P = f instead of P = 1/f.

recall.must_convey: That the power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length, P = 1/f with f in metre.
accept: power is one by focal length
P equals one by f with f in metres

steps.memory_tip: Short focal length, strong lens: P and f are reciprocals.

steps.label: Unit: dioptre
lines: The SI unit of power of a lens is the
It is the power of a lens of focal length
1 metre. For a convex lens f is positive,
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the dioptre and define it: the power of a lens of focal length one metre.
steps.why: Naming the unit earns only half the point of this mark — defining it (1 D is the power when f = 1 m) is what shows the unit was understood and not memorised.
common_mistakes: Writing watt for the unit. The dioptre, not the watt, is the unit of lens power.
Leaving the sign unstated. A convex lens has positive f, so its power is positive.

recall.must_convey: That the unit is the dioptre, the power of a lens whose focal length is one metre.
accept: one dioptre is one metre inverse
dioptre means focal length of one metre
reject: power is one by focal length

steps.memory_tip: Dioptre = the one-metre lens: f = 1 m gives P = 1 D.

insider_note: The examiner looks for two things: the reciprocal relation with f in metre, and the dioptre named AND defined.
